notes: Fixes a fresh install. Columns added by later migrations (queue visit type, consultation price, and the scanner fields from an earlier version) were applied by ALTER statements that run before those tables are created, so on a brand new database they failed silently and the columns were missing — adding a patient to the queue or saving settings then failed with "no such column". Existing databases were unaffected, which is why it only appeared on a new setup. The columns are now part of the table definitions as well as the migrations.
